title: Eosinophil-count curvature does not establish incremental cross-cycle prediction of elevated CRP beyond standard leukocyte and adiposity measures
abstract: A frozen quadratic term in discovery-centered log blood eosinophil count was added to standard demographic, adiposity and leukocyte predictors of single-visit CRP >3 mg/L. Logistic models trained in 5,069 NHANES 2007–2008 adults were evaluated without refitting in 4,639 separately recruited 2017–2018 adults. Survey-weighted Brier score changed by +0.0000417 (95% fixed-model stratified PSU bootstrap interval −0.0000130 to +0.0000915; delete-PSU normal interval −0.0000324 to +0.0001158). The prespecified improvement was not established. Restriction and penalty sensitivities sometimes favored curvature; this is not evidence of universal absence of eosinophil information. Shared survey infrastructure, assay changes and complete-case selection limit externality. Code, provenance, predictions and author self-checks are provided.
